newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares surge, up nine days in a row.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares surge, up nine days in a row.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 1.44 percent on Friday to end out the week 8.9 percent higher and up nine days in a row.
Traders said more gains could be expected due to mounting optimism.
"The feeling on the market is good as many investors have regained their confidence in shares and are coming back," said Nina Jarc, a trader of bank Nova Ljubljanska banka.
Traders cited investor demand for shares in bank SKB, drug company Lek and food maker Kolinska, all posted good half-year results.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 15.54 points to 1,097.12.
* 10 shares rose and six fell, while eight were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 560 million tolars from 309.7 million.
* Bank SKB had the highest turnover, rising 4.84 percent to 34,593 tolars on volume of 7,319 shares for total turnover of 253.2 million tolars.
* Preferred shares of trader Kovinotehna were the top gainers, rising 5.52 percent to 428.7 on volume of 1,290 shares for total turnover of 0.6 million tolars.

* Bank Hipotekarna banka Brezice was the leading decliner. Its shares fell 8.55 percent to 3,151 on volume of 20 shares for total turnover of 0.06 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
